title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness

release_status.value: Complete official HITCH code, teacher trajectories, and policy weights were not verified; the project page could not be reviewed.

evidence_boundaries: The VLM emits one structured call per turn. A command runs to completion before the next observation.
50 Hz denotes HEFT tracking, not VLM query rate.
Five-shot results use supervised model fine-tuning and simulation, not in-context examples or real trials.
SIMPLE covers six tasks and HumanoidArena covers four. Camera, execution stack and instruction wording are adapted.
The five-shot control uses a different training duration. When there are multiple saved checkpoints, the paper selects by SIMPLE success.
Tracker comparison is under the HITCH command/reference distribution and code teachers, not a general tracker ranking.
Hardware has rubber palms without finger control. Only two real tasks are tested.
The planner supports flat walking, reaching, leaning and crouching. Fast within-command reactions and other motions are outside its evaluated scope.
